label: late copy phase, fed-back token p/j/2/r
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>), and only at late absolute steps: essentially zero before t=8, with rate rising toward t=16-17. So it is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 69% of mass) and at recall_idx>=3. It is strongly token-selective on the copy-phase input (the previously emitted token): p (10.7x lift, 43% of mass, and most top activations, e.g. ...p at step 16), then j, 2, r, with weaker h/3/g. Within copy, rate grows with the number of digits in the sequence. It never fires on a first occurrence of a token. The predicate (late copy step with input p/j/2/r) captures ~74% of activation mass but has low precision (~24%): most late-copy p/j/2/r steps stay inactive. Adding digit count, repeat count, or to_go conditions did not raise F1 above ~0.36, so an unidentified hidden-state factor still decides whether it fires. Larger activations are enriched for input p at the latest steps.
